The proposed pre-consent pilot could be integrated into existing touchpoints like prenatal appointments. Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems. The proposal includes a planned small-scale test of a 'decline feedback' channel, asking beneficiaries who decline automated offers to optionally share their reasons, to improve targeting and communication. Furthermore, the proposal includes a planned small, targeted test of a 'pre-emptive information' channel. This test would send a brief, plain-language summary of data usage and privacy safeguards alongside the initial offer message, aiming to build trust and increase opt-in rates. Additionally, the proposal includes a planned, small-scale test of a 'reverse notification' feature. This would allow users to proactively and securely flag a life event (e.g., job loss) within the government app to trigger the automated eligibility check, providing a bridge for events not automatically captured by registration systems. This proposed test of the 'reverse notification' feature would also include integrating it with a secure, verifiable document upload function for the single most common missing document (e.g., a termination letter), to bridge the gap for events not fully captured in government records. The proposed test would also include a 'life event confirmation receipt' that users can save or share, providing them with a tangible record of their proactive notification to the government. The proposal also includes a planned small-scale test of a 'trusted intermediary' consent model. In this test, a citizen could authorize a pre-vetted community organization (e.g., a local family center) to receive and help them understand the automated offer on their behalf, specifically for non-digital users.

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A proposed enhancement to this model is a hypothetical partnership with a select number of trusted, non-governmental community organizations to act as 'digital navigators' for the phone line and service centers. These navigators would specifically assist non-digital users in understanding and responding to the automated offers, thereby testing an enhanced inclusion model.
